conversation.content:
Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant journey you've been on, becoming a new mother. This can be a time of great joy, but also of adjustment and uncertainty. As we navigate this postpartum period together, I want to assure you that everything discussed in this room will remain confidential and respected.

Today, I'll be using the EPDS to assess how you're feeling and to better understand your postpartum experience. The EPDS is a tool that helps us screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, which can be common during this time. It's essential to remember that experiencing emotional changes after giving birth is normal, and this assessment is here to support you, not to judge.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us understand your feelings and thoughts over the past week. I'll ask you these questions one by one, and you can share as much or as little as you feel comfortable with. Please know that you're in a safe and supportive space, and I'm here to listen and provide guidance without judgment.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that your well-being and safety are my top priority. If at any point during our conversation you feel overwhelmed or need immediate support, please don't hesitate to let me know.

Now, let's get started with the first question. Over the past week, how have you been feeling about yourself? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually like doing, or have you been feeling somewhat withdrawn or disconnected from activities that bring you joy?

.. to be honest, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and tired most of the time. I mean, I love my baby, and I'm so grateful to be a mom, but it's just been really hard to enjoy the things I used to like doing. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby and the house, but I'm not really feeling any joy or excitement about it. Sometimes I'll be doing something with the baby, like feeding or bathing, and I'll think to myself, "This should be a special moment, but I just feel so empty and tired." 

I do try to do some things that I used to enjoy, like reading or watching TV, but even those things don't seem to bring me as much pleasure as they used to. And some days, I just feel really sad and discouraged, like I'm not doing a good enough job as a mom. I worry that I'm not giving my baby the best possible start in life, and that thought can be really overwhelming for me. But, I mean, I'm trying to stay positive and focus on the good things, like how much I love my baby and how lucky I am to have her. It's just... it's hard, you know.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

.. I don't know if I've been able to laugh as much as I used to. I mean, sometimes my husband will try to make me laugh, and I'll smile or chuckle, but it's not the same as it used to be. It feels like it's all just a bit of an effort, you know? Like, I'm trying to be happy and laugh, but it's just not coming as naturally as it used to. 

And as for seeing the funny side of things... I don't know, it's like my perspective has changed or something. I'll be in the middle of a chaotic moment, like when the baby is crying and I'm trying to make dinner, and I'll think to myself, "This is just crazy, I should be laughing about this," but instead, I just feel anxious and overwhelmed. I feel like I'm just trying to survive each day, rather than actually enjoying it or finding the humor in things. 

It's weird, because I used to be a pretty positive person, and I used to be able to laugh at myself and find the humor in tough situations. But now, it just feels like everything is so serious and overwhelming, and I don't know how to get back to that carefree, laughing person I used to be.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

.. to be honest, I haven't really been looking forward to things like I used to. I mean, I'll have plans to do something, like go for a walk or meet a friend, and at first, I'll think, "Oh, that sounds nice," but then as the day gets closer, I'll start to feel anxious and overwhelmed. I'll think about all the things I need to do to get ready, like getting the baby dressed and fed, and just the thought of it all feels exhausting.

And even when I do manage to get out and do something, I don't always enjoy it as much as I thought I would. Like, I'll be out with my friend, and I'll be thinking about the baby the whole time, worrying about whether she's okay, or whether I've forgotten something important. It's hard to just relax and enjoy the moment, you know?

I've also been having trouble sleeping, which makes it hard for me to look forward to things. I'll lie awake at night, thinking about all the things I need to do the next day, and worrying about whether I'll be able to get everything done. It's like my mind is always racing, and I just can't seem to calm down.

Sometimes, I'll catch myself thinking about how much I used to enjoy certain activities, like reading or watching a movie, but now they just feel like chores. I'll think, "I should be enjoying this," but it just doesn't feel the same. It's like I've lost my sense of pleasure and enjoyment, and I don't know how to get it back.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that I just don't feel like myself anymore. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really living. And that's a hard thing to admit, because I feel like I should be grateful for this beautiful baby and this new life, but it's just not feeling that way right now.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I do that a lot, actually. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If the baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If she's not sleeping well, I think it's because I didn't establish a good routine. If she's not eating well, I think it's because I'm not making the right food choices. It's like I'm always questioning my own abilities as a mother, and I feel like I'm just waiting for something to go wrong so I can say, "See, I knew I wasn't doing this right."

And it's not just with the baby, either. I'll be doing something around the house, and I'll make a mistake, and I'll think, "Why am I so careless? Why can't I just get it together?" It's like I'm always criticizing myself, and it's really hard to shake that feeling.

I remember one day, I was trying to get the baby to nap, and I was rocking her and singing to her, and she just wouldn't settle down. And I started to feel so frustrated and anxious, and I thought to myself, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I even get my own baby to sleep?" It was like I was failing as a mother, and it was all my fault.

It's hard to explain, but it's like I have this constant voice in my head that's always telling me that I'm not good enough, that I'm not doing things right. And it's exhausting, because I feel like I'm always trying to prove myself, to myself, and to others. And I just wish I could stop being so hard on myself, you know? I wish I could just be kind to myself, and say, "It's okay, I'm doing the best I can." But it's hard to do that when I'm always feeling so guilty and self-critical.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

.. yes. I've been feeling really anxious and worried a lot lately, and it's hard to explain why. I mean, everything seems to be okay, the baby is healthy, my husband is supportive, but I just can't shake this feeling of worry and unease. It's like I'm always waiting for something to go wrong, and I don't know what it is or when it's going to happen, but I just feel like I'm on edge all the time.

Sometimes it's about the baby, like I'll be thinking about all the things that could go wrong, like SIDS or accidents or illnesses. And I'll be lying awake at night, thinking about all these worst-case scenarios, and I just can't calm down. I'll be thinking, "What if I'm not doing enough to protect her? What if I'm not giving her the best possible start in life?" And it's just this constant, nagging worry that I don't know how to get rid of.

And it's not just about the baby, either. I'll be doing everyday things, like grocery shopping or cooking dinner, and I'll start to feel this sense of anxiety and unease. I'll be thinking, "What if I forget something important? What if I'm not doing this right?" It's like I'm always second-guessing myself, and it's just exhausting.

I've also been having trouble sleeping, which makes the anxiety worse. I'll lie awake at night, thinking about all my worries, and I just can't seem to calm down. I've had a few nights where I've woken up in a panic, thinking about something that's been worrying me, and I just can't get back to sleep. It's like my mind is always racing, and I don't know how to slow it down.

I've even had some fleeting thoughts of self-harm, just because I feel so overwhelmed and anxious all the time. It's like I'm just trying to survive each day, rather than actually living. And that's a really scary feeling, because I don't know how to make it stop. I just feel like I'm losing control, and I don't know how to get it back.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that I just feel really overwhelmed and anxious all the time, and I don't know how to make it stop. I feel like I'm just waiting for something to go wrong, and I don't know how to calm down and just enjoy the present moment. It's like I'm stuck in this constant state of worry and fear, and I don't know how to escape.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... I've been feeling that way a lot lately. I'll be doing something completely normal, like feeding the baby or taking a shower, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, my breath will get short, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. It's like my body is reacting to some kind of threat, but there's no actual danger there.

Sometimes it's triggered by something specific, like a loud noise or a sudden movement, but other times it just comes out of nowhere. I'll be sitting on the couch, feeding the baby, and suddenly I'll feel this overwhelming sense of fear and panic. It's like my mind is playing tricks on me, making me think that something terrible is happening, even when it's not.

It's hard to explain, but it's like my body is constantly on high alert, waiting for something to go wrong. And when that panic sets in, it's hard to calm down. I'll try to breathe deeply, or distract myself with something else, but it's hard to shake the feeling of fear and anxiety.

Sometimes, when I'm feeling really overwhelmed, I'll have these thoughts of "What if I'm not a good enough mom?" or "What if something happens to the baby?" And those thoughts will just spiral out of control, making me feel even more panicked and scared. It's like I'm trapped in this cycle of fear and anxiety, and I don't know how to escape.

It's also hard because I feel like I'm supposed to be this strong, capable mom, but inside, I'm just feeling so scared and uncertain. I feel like I'm just pretending to be okay, when really, I'm just barely holding it together. And that feeling of pretending, of not being honest about how I'm really feeling, it just adds to the anxiety and panic.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that I just feel really scared and panicky a lot of the time, and I don't know how to make it stop. I feel like I'm just waiting for something to go wrong, and I don't know how to calm down and just enjoy the present moment. It's like I'm stuck in this constant state of fear and anxiety, and I don't know how to escape.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's definitely true. I feel like things have been getting on top of me for a while now. Being a new mom is just so overwhelming, and it feels like there's always something that needs to be done. Whether it's feeding the baby, changing diapers, or just trying to keep the house clean, it's like there's always something demanding my attention.

And it's not just the practical things, either. Emotionally, I feel like I'm just barely keeping my head above water. I'm constantly worried about the baby's health, and whether I'm doing everything right. I'm worried about my relationship with my husband, and whether we're going to be able to navigate this new chapter in our lives together. I'm worried about my own identity, and whether I've lost myself in all of this.

Sometimes it feels like everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to cope. I'll be sitting on the couch, feeding the baby, and I'll just start to feel this sense of overwhelm and anxiety. It's like I'm drowning in a sea of responsibility, and I don't know how to keep my head above water.

I've been trying to manage my anxiety by taking things one step at a time, and focusing on the present moment. But it's hard, because my mind is always racing ahead to the next thing, the next worry, the next problem to solve. And it's exhausting, because I feel like I'm always "on", always alert, always waiting for the next thing to go wrong.

I've also been having trouble sleeping, which doesn't help. I'll lie awake at night, thinking about all the things I need to do, and worrying about everything that could go wrong. And when I do finally fall asleep, I'll have these vivid dreams that are just filled with anxiety and fear. It's like my mind is just constantly racing, even when I'm supposed to be resting.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that, yes, things have been getting on top of me. I feel like I'm just barely keeping my head above water, and I don't know how to keep going. I feel like I need some help, some support, some way to manage all of these emotions and responsibilities that are just piling up on me.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up all the time. I mean, that's definitely a part of it, but even when she's sleeping through the night, I'm still lying awake, feeling anxious and unhappy.

It's like my mind is just racing all the time, thinking about all the things that could go wrong, all the things I'm not doing right, all the things I'm worried about. And it's hard to shut it off, you know? I'll be lying there, feeling exhausted, but my mind is just going a mile a minute, thinking about everything that's stressing me out.

And it's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, it's the quality of sleep too. Even when I do fall asleep, I'm having these vivid dreams that are just filled with anxiety and fear. I'll wake up feeling more tired than when I went to bed, because my mind has been racing all night, processing all my worries and fears.

Sometimes I'll wake up in the middle of the night, feeling just overwhelmed with sadness and anxiety. I'll be lying there, feeling like I'm just drowning in my emotions, and I don't know how to keep going. It's like I'm just barely holding on, you know?

And it's not just the nighttime, either. During the day, I'll be feeling okay, and then suddenly I'll just start crying. I'll be feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and I'll just start sobbing. It's like all my emotions are just right there, on the surface, and it's hard to keep them under control.

I've been trying to talk to my husband about it, but it's hard to explain. He's been really supportive, but I feel like he doesn't really get it. He'll say things like, "Just try to relax," or "You're doing a great job," but it's not that easy. It's not just about relaxing, or doing a good job. It's about feeling like I'm just barely holding on, and I don't know how much longer I can keep going.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that, yes, I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because of the baby. It's because of all the emotions that are swirling around inside me, all the worries and fears that are keeping me up at night. I feel like I need some help, some support, some way to manage all of these emotions and get some rest.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... I've been feeling that way a lot lately. It's like a cloud of sadness is just following me around all the time. I'll be doing something with the baby, and I'll just start to feel this overwhelming sense of sadness and misery. It's like I'm grieving the loss of my old life, my old self. I feel like I've lost my identity, my sense of purpose.

Sometimes it's just a dull ache, a feeling of emptiness and hollowness. Other times it's a intense, overwhelming sadness that just feels like it's going to consume me. I'll be sitting on the couch, holding the baby, and I'll just start to cry. It's like the tears are just pouring out of me, and I don't know how to stop them.

It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just feeling so much pain and sadness all the time. It's like my heart is just heavy, weighed down by all these emotions. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. I'll be doing laundry, or cooking dinner, and I'll just start to feel this wave of sadness wash over me.

I've been trying to talk to my husband about it, but it's hard to put into words. He's been really supportive, but I feel like he doesn't really get it. He'll say things like, "You're just tired," or "You're just adjusting to motherhood," but it's more than that. It's like I'm just feeling this deep, profound sadness that I don't know how to escape.

Sometimes I'll have these moments of feeling okay, of feeling like I'm getting my footing as a mom. But then something will happen, and I'll just feel like I'm right back where I started. It's like I'm just taking two steps forward, and then three steps back.

I've also been having these thoughts of self-doubt, these feelings of guilt and shame. I'll be thinking, "I'm not a good enough mom," or "I'm not doing this right." And it's hard to shake those thoughts, hard to remind myself that I'm doing the best I can.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that, yes, I've been feeling sad and miserable a lot lately. It's like this cloud of sadness is just following me around, and I don't know how to make it go away. I feel like I need some help, some support, some way to work through all these emotions and find some peace.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like the tears are just always right there, waiting to spill out. I'll be doing something with the baby, or just sitting on the couch, and I'll just start to feel this overwhelming sense of sadness and emotion. And then the tears will just start to flow.

It's not just a little crying, either. I mean, it's not just a few tears here and there. It's like full-on, sobbing, can't-catch-my-breath crying. It's like my body is just releasing all this pent-up emotion, and I don't know how to stop it.

Sometimes it's triggered by something specific, like a argument with my husband or a difficult moment with the baby. But other times, it's just out of nowhere. I'll be doing something completely mundane, like folding laundry or washing dishes, and I'll just start to feel this wave of sadness wash over me. And then the tears will start to flow.

It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just feeling so much emotion all the time. I'm feeling overwhelmed and anxious and sad, and it's all just bubbling up to the surface. And when I cry, it's like my body is just releasing all that tension and emotion.

I've been trying to hide it from my husband, but it's hard. He'll see me crying, and he'll try to comfort me, but it's hard to explain. He'll say things like, "What's wrong?" or "Is everything okay?" And I'll just shake my head, because I don't know how to put it into words.

Sometimes I'll cry when the baby is crying, too. It's like we're just both overwhelmed and emotional, and we're feeding off each other's energy. And it's hard, because I feel like I should be the strong one, the one who's calming the baby down. But instead, I'm just crying right along with her.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that, yes, I've been crying a lot lately. It's like my emotions are just always right on the surface, and I don't know how to keep them from spilling out. I feel like I need some help, some support, some way to work through all these emotions and find some peace.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

I... I don't know if I should be saying this, but... yes. The thought of harming myself has occurred to me. It's like, sometimes I feel so overwhelmed and anxious and sad, and I just don't know how to make it stop. And in those moments, I've had thoughts of... of just wanting to escape, I guess. Of wanting to make the pain go away.

It's not like I've actually planned anything or taken any steps to harm myself. It's just... it's just these fleeting thoughts that come into my head when I'm feeling really overwhelmed. And they're scary, because I don't know where they're coming from or how to make them go away.

I feel like I'm just barely holding on, you know? Like, I'm just trying to survive each day, and I don't know how much longer I can keep going. And in those moments, the thought of harming myself is just... it's just there. It's like, maybe if I just didn't exist anymore, all this pain and sadness would go away.

But at the same time, I know that's not true. I know that there are people who care about me, who love me, and who want to help me. And I know that I have a baby who needs me, who depends on me. So, I don't know... I just don't know what to do with these thoughts, I guess.

It's hard to talk about this, because it feels so... so shameful, I guess. Like, I'm a bad person for even thinking these things. But at the same time, I know that I need to talk about it, because I need help. I need someone to talk to, someone who can help me work through these feelings and find a way to make them go away.

I'm just so tired of feeling this way, I guess. I'm tired of feeling like I'm just barely holding on, like I'm just waiting for something to go wrong. I want to feel like myself again, like I'm in control of my life and my emotions. But right now, I just don't know how to get there.
